title: Web Technologies Lecture 2: Event Listeners, Event Bubbling & Event Capturing
routing_rationale: PDI=0.500 < 0.60: Material is predominantly static, code-dense, or monologue exposition. Routed to Technical Summary.

questions.question_text: In the context of DOM manipulation, which statement accurately defines an event listener?
questions.option_a: It is the specific user action (such as a click or keypress) that triggers a change in the browser's state.
questions.option_b: It is a function registered to a specific DOM element that executes in response to a specific event.
questions.option_c: It is a global variable attached to the document root that monitors all user interactions across the entire page.
questions.option_d: It is a CSS property that defines the visual feedback displayed when a user hovers over an interactive element.
questions.explanation: Option B is correct because an event listener is fundamentally a callback function attached to an element (via methods like addEventListener) that runs when a specified event occurs. Option A is incorrect because it describes the 'event' itself, not the listener. Option C is incorrect because listeners can be attached to any element, not just the document root, and they are not global variables. Option D is incorrect because it confuses JavaScript event handling with CSS pseudo-classes.
questions.what_taught: An event listener is a function registered to a DOM element that executes in response to a specific event.
questions.why_assessed: Establishes the foundational vocabulary and mechanism for all subsequent event handling concepts.
questions.misconception_rationale: Distractor A targets the misconception of confusing the event object/action with the listener function. Distractor C targets the misconception that event handling is limited to the document root or is a global state. Distractor D targets the confusion between JavaScript logic and CSS styling mechanisms.
